purpose: Teach Film Studio that a contained result at a cheaper liquid tier cannot clear an accepted defect observed at a more discriminating tier, and make it select the smallest same-tier single-variable probe instead of silently passing.

allowed: modify only scripts/modules/film_studio_fluid_pipeline.py on the retained product branch
run pure system-Python validation and independent audit without Blender
publish research evidence and an ordinary fast-forward product commit after PASS
forbidden: Blender start, bake, render, build or scene mutation
force push, tag, release, binary distribution or paid service

productContract.inputAuthority: The product supplies exact self-hashed accepted-defect and candidate-observation receipts; a proposal cannot supply a verdict, next tier or action.
requiredBindings: same metric identifier and threshold semantics

decisionRules.condition: candidate tier is cheaper than the accepted defect tier and candidate is contained
candidate tier equals the accepted defect tier, candidate is contained and exactly one parameter changed
candidate still exceeds the defect threshold at the same tier

requiredNegativeTests: resolution not equal to product-owned tier resolution
candidate tier above accepted defect tier
caller-supplied verdict, next action or clears-defect field
stopRule: Stop before product mutation if the research parent, product commit, branch, module path or bound evidence differs. Stop during implementation on a second changed product path, any Blender/build/bake/render/network process, any caller-authored decision field, any accepted-defect-clearing output, an input not bound to exact physics/metric/threshold identity, a non-finite value, a changed-parameter roster other than exactly one, or a failing positive/negative case.
claimCeiling: A PASS proves one pure decision function prevents a cheaper liquid tier from clearing an accepted higher-tier defect and selects the smallest same-tier single-variable probe. It does not prove the present Final correction, reconstructed surface, slow tip, impact, render, runtime speedup or finished-film quality.
